name: Chester County, Pennsylvania (United States)
description: White field charged with a map of the county divided in three with the elements of the Pennsylvania arms — a ship, a plough and wheat sheaves — under an eagle and between branches, with the date 1682.
history: Chester County, colloquially referred to as Chesco, is a county in Pennsylvania. The flag was adopted on 26 October 1982 (designed by Jan Trembley of West Goshen Township, winner of a residents' contest, and first dedicated on 26 October 1982 at the courthouse for the county's tricentennial, according to Flags of the World citing the Tredyffrin Easttown Historical Society).

features.role: map of the county bearing the elements of the Pennsylvania arms
